{{Quote|Greetings. In the equation A <nowiki>= (</nowiki>&pi;<nowiki>/</nowiki>1012 &times; 16,072<nowiki>)(</nowiki>R&times;R<nowiki>)(</nowiki>E&infin;<nowiki>)</nowiki>&sup2;, can you tell me what the value of A is?|A Givin|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>}}
The '''Givin''' were the indigenous [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]]. They were best known for their natural mathematical ability which made them expert [[Starship/Legends|starship]] builders and [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogators]]. Other notable features of the Givin were their skeletal appearance, and their ability to survive in a [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Givin_2.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Givin]]

Givin appeared to be living [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] skeletons, because of their hard, pale white "skin" and deep sunken black eyes.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /> Though they had four-<ref name="Action figure">[[Elis Helrot/Legends|Elis Helrot]] action figure</ref> or five-fingered hands,<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /> they had three-toed feet.<ref name="Action figure" /> They carried their arms and legs "held out" from their bodies, making their appearance even more bizarre. Some likened their stance to [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] string puppets.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" />

Due to a complex system of [[Moon/Legends|moons]] that created atmospheric tidal upheavals on Yag'Dhul, the Givin evolved a hard exoskeleton that could seal all external orifices to protect against sudden depressurization and temperature changes. It also provided protection from physical harm. Thus, Givin had a phobia of exposed skin, and would avoid seeing it in others whenever possible. In order to maintain this sealed system, Givin needed to eat approximately three times more than [[Human/Legends|Humans]] of the same mass. Givin could easily survive in a total vacuum for a standard day.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" />

==Culture==
Givin were highly intelligent, and had such a propensity for mathematics that their society was ruled over by a mathematical theocracy, or mathematocracy, with the greatest mathematicians serving in the ruling [[Body Calculus]].<ref name="Yag'Dhul Secedes">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|regional/1352_1.html|Yag'Dhul Secedes}}</ref> Their mathematical skills were, like their sealed exoskeletons, adaptations to Yag'Dhul's complex tidal systems&mdash;their mathematics were developed to predict Yag'Dhul's randomly shifting oceans and atmosphere. The planetary governor of Yag'Dhul was decided by contests that involved calculations of complex multidimensional differentials, and all political decisions were based on null-modal probability.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /><ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>

They created some of the most impressive, complex, and sleek ships in the galaxy. Often, other species would need to modify a purchased Givin starship, installing a [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]] or pressurization system which would often be left out as unnecessary by the Givin, who could survive in a vacuum and mentally calculated navigational vectors.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /><ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

===Sample Givin names===
*Lersia Narth
*Na-Soth Larr
*Nisil Alarin
*Daggibus Scoritoles
*Sladru Nalas

==History==
[[File:Givin-GOI.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The skeletal face of a Givin]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Givin lent their mathematical, engineering, and navigational talents to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]],<ref name="Givin">{{DB|species|givin|Givin}}</ref> producing such designs as the [[Wavecrest-class frigate|''Wavecrest''-class frigates]].<ref name="CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:3:21 Edition">{{InsiderCite|76|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:3:21 Edition}}</ref> By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Givin shipbuilding industry had recovered and was producing highly advanced ships for both military and civilian purposes. Yag'Dhul was attacked once by the Yuuzhan Vong, but never again. Afterward, ambassadors to the planet made sure they underwent extensive education in mathematics before negotiating with the Givin.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Givin in the galaxy==
While they respected other shipbuilding species such as the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]] and the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], they disliked the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] due to differences in design philosophy. They also tended to be subtly arrogant toward other species who could not survive in a vacuum ([[Duinuogwuin/Legends|Duinuogwuin]] being the major exception).<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Finally, since non-Givin often failed to solve the simple quadratic equations used as introductions in polite Givin society, Givin found most aliens to be rather rude.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /><ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Behind the scenes==
According to the [[Elis Helrot]] action figure by [[Hasbro]], the Givin physiology features three-toed feet.

The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] refers to the species as "Yag'Duhls."
